title: Jacob Kiplimo Wins Third Straight World XC Title
excerpt: Jacob Kiplimo won the 2026 World Cross Country title in 28:18, 18 seconds clear, for his third straight win. Lessons on timing a race-winning move.
body:
Uganda's Jacob Kiplimo won the senior men's race at the 2026 World Athletics Cross Country Championships in Tallahassee on January 10 in 28:18. He finished 18 seconds ahead of Ethiopia's Berihu Aregawi (28:36), with Kenya's Daniel Simiu Ebenyo third (28:45). It was Kiplimo's third consecutive world cross country title, after 2023 and 2024. Ethiopia won the team title ahead of Kenya and Uganda.

A winning margin like that comes from fitness and from committing fully once a move is made. Most races are decided by when runners choose to push, not only by how fit they are.

In your next tempo run or race, pick a landmark about two-thirds of the way through and make a deliberate decision there: hold your pace, push, or back off. Making that a habit in training builds the race awareness you need when it counts.

Sources: LetsRun.com; World Athletics
keyTakeaway: Practise deciding in advance where in a race you will commit to a harder effort.
